text.p: Italian bond futures rose steadily throughout the day helped by the firmer trend on other world bond markets especially U.S. Treasuries and encouraging words from the government on progress towards ERM and EMU membership.
"The market was watching Treasuries and the progress of the lira, and what Prodi and Ciampi said gave the market some comfort," said one trader on the LIFFE market.

Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Italy intended to return to the ERM by the end of 1996, while Prime Minister Romano Prodi reported that German Chancellor Helmut Kohl had said Italy will make rapid and effective progress towards EMU.

Dealers said the Italian August PPI/WPI data out earlier was encouraging for the market with wholesale inflation at just 2.0 percent year-on-year against a rise of 2.6 percent in July, and producer prices unchanged at zero percent.
They pointed out that most bond market around the world were generally firmer today, with BTP contracts watching firmer bunds early then taking support from Treasuries.
"The optimism has returned to Italy, and investors are pushing budget worries and EMU concerns onto the backburner for the moment," said the LIFFE trader.
